scope_summary: A + B (small): subagent fan-out inside reviewer_code (option A) plus two new ADVISORY reviewer roles reviewer_security and reviewer_concurrency (option B). Threshold-gated (~10 files OR ~500 LOC), reviewer self-gates the threshold (decision-1 = 2B), reviewer self-fetches the implement-phase task list via mcp__sdlc__show_contract (decision-2 = 3B), partition-by-subsystem, subagents re-run git diff filtered by path glob (decision-4), criteria files inherit from code-review-criteria.md (decision-5), per-pipeline parallelism knob lives at phase_configs.implement.reviewer_code.parallel (decision-6), regression test ships with both prompt-asserts (CI-unconditional) and live-LLM replay gated by RUN_REVIEWER_REPLAY=1 (decision-7).
third_party_external_research: Skipped per task instructions: this change is purely internal to the egg orchestrator/sandbox. The only third-party touch points are (a) the Anthropic Claude Agent SDK's built-in Task subagent tool already bundled in shared/egg_agent/client.py and (b) the existing python-sdk dependency footprint. No new package adoption, no new vulnerable surface, no new vendored dependency. Existing SDK risks (rate limits, prompt-injection from diff content) are inherited rather than introduced.

risks.title: Subagent fan-out fires for non-implement-phase reviewers if not phase-gated
risks.evidence: orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py builds reviewer prompts via _build_review_prompt() and dispatches inside _build_agent_prompt() with a single guard `elif role_value.startswith("reviewer_")` (line ~8315). There is no per-phase guard inside the reviewer_code branch today. The new subagent block sits inside reviewer_code procedural steps; if a future plan-phase or refine-phase contract were ever to assign reviewer_code (or if one of the new reviewers were registered for refine/plan by mistake), the implement-phase fan-out instructions would leak into prose-review prompts and cause garbage subagent spawns.
risks.mitigation: Wrap the subagent fan-out block in an explicit `if phase == "implement"` guard inside the reviewer_code branch of _build_review_prompt(). Add a unit test that builds the prompt for reviewer_code in (refine, plan, implement) phases and asserts the subagent block is present iff phase == implement. Also keep the new reviewer roles registered in shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py only against PipelinePhase.IMPLEMENT in _PHASE_REVIEWERS so role assignment cannot cross phases.
risks.rollback: Revert the prompt change in pipelines.py — pure prompt text, no schema, no on-disk state. Rollback is a single-commit revert with no migration.

risks.title: Reviewer self-gating threshold (option 2B) is non-deterministic and invisible to telemetry
risks.evidence: Decision-1 chose option 2B: reviewer reads `git diff --numstat` itself and decides fan-out vs solo review. The reviewer is an LLM; it may miscount, misinterpret "OR" composition (decision-3), or skip the gate entirely under prompt-pressure. Telemetry today has no per-pipeline counter for fan-out fired vs skipped, so silent regressions (e.g., reviewer always solos because the prompt format drifted) won't surface until the GHA reviewer catches missed issues again.
risks.mitigation: (1) Embed a single-line STATUS instruction the reviewer must emit before reviewing — e.g., `egg-orch message send --to all --type STATUS --subject "reviewer_code fan-out: <enabled|skipped> (files=<N>, loc=<M>)"`. The orchestrator can grep STATUS messages in BRC history later. (2) Make the threshold rule a single short paragraph in the prompt — files>10 OR loc>500 → fan out — to minimise misinterpretation. (3) The decision-7 prompt-text regression test should assert this paragraph is present and well-formed; a snapshot-style test catches drift cheaply. (4) Plan a follow-up issue to add Python-side numstat instrumentation if telemetry shows >10 percent gate-misfires.
risks.rollback: If reviewer self-gating proves unreliable in practice, switch to option 2A (orchestrator-side numstat plumbing) without changing any contract schema — the prompt instructions become a fallback. Cost is ~50 LOC of plumbing in _get_reviewer_scope_preamble plus the call site in _build_review_prompt.

risks.title: Reviewer self-fetched implement task list (option 3B) couples reviewer prompts to contract internals and adds an MCP failure mode
risks.evidence: Decision-2 chose option 3B: reviewer calls mcp__sdlc__show_contract and self-extracts phases.implement.tasks[]. The contract schema is governed by shared/egg_contracts/models.py and .egg/schemas/contract.schema.json; if `phases.implement.tasks` is renamed or restructured (e.g., a wrapping object keyed by task id), the reviewer prompt's extraction path silently breaks and falls back to `skip fan-out` — a silent regression. There is also no precedent in this repo for Task subagents calling MCP servers; subagent execution context (cwd, env vars including EGG_AGENT_ROLE, MCP server config) has not been validated end-to-end.
risks.mitigation: (1) The plan must mandate a smoke test that confirms `Task` subagents inherit MCP server access in the sandbox; this is decision-10's entire premise. If the smoke test fails, decision-10's "primarily a prompt change" framing collapses and the work expands. (2) Pin the contract extraction path in a single helper instruction inside the reviewer prompt (e.g., "call mcp__sdlc__show_contract; the implement-phase task list lives at result['contract']['phases'][i] where phases[i].id == 'implement'; fall back to skip-fan-out if absent"). (3) Ship a fallback that explicitly says "if mcp__sdlc__show_contract returns no implement-phase tasks, partition by changed-file directory instead of subsystem" — preserves fan-out value when the contract is empty. (4) Add a `egg-contract` schema-version field check at the top of the helper paragraph so future schema migrations fail loudly rather than silently.
risks.rollback: Switch to option 3A (orchestrator-side contract loader). Adds a `contract` (or `pipeline_id`) parameter to _build_review_prompt; existing callers already have access to the contract object near the call site (line ~8318). Reversal cost is medium (~80 LOC + parameter threading) but contained to one file.

risks.title: Task subagent execution model is unproven in this repo; first production use
risks.evidence: Codebase grep confirms the Claude Agent SDK Task tool is referenced only in documentation strings inside orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py (lines ~6902-6920, ~8064-8065) telling coder/tester they may use it. There is no production code path that has actually exercised Task subagents end-to-end in egg. shared/egg_agent/client.py:162-167 only blocks WebFetch/WebSearch in private mode; Task is not blocked, but "not blocked" does not equal "verified working with MCP server access, EGG_AGENT_ROLE inheritance, restricted-path push enforcement, and concurrent-mode telemetry". Unknown unknowns include subagent error propagation (parent ACK on subagent failure?), token-limit behaviour on 12-file fan-outs, and whether subagents can deadlock the parent's BRC heartbeat by holding the event loop.
risks.mitigation: (1) Plan must include a pre-implementation spike: a throwaway smoke pipeline in dev that spawns 2-3 subagents from reviewer_code to confirm MCP reachability, env-var inheritance, write-block enforcement, and parent-context return semantics. (2) The implementation task that adds the subagent block must include a structured logging hook — when the parent reviewer fans out, log subagent count, partition spec, and per-subagent verdict to a structured field in the BRC ACK. (3) Land the change behind decision-6's `phase_configs.implement.reviewer_code.parallel` flag *defaulted to false* on the first PR, then flip the default to true in a second PR after at least one full implement-phase BRC cycle has exercised the path successfully. (4) Document subagent verdict-merging semantics explicitly: parent reviewer ACKs only if every subagent ACKs; any subagent NACK becomes a parent NACK.
risks.rollback: Set the new contract field default to false (subagents off) — reverts behaviour to today's solo-reviewer path with zero schema change. The criteria-file plumbing and ADVISORY reviewer additions remain operational.

risks.title: Adding REVIEWER_ATTESTATION_MODELS entries by reflex would break ADVISORY reviewers that ACK without attestation
risks.evidence: orchestrator/peer_consensus.py:289-291 calls validate_attestation only when `review.attestation` is truthy. orchestrator/attestation_schemas.py:227-228 raises ValueError if there is no model for the role. The two existing model-less reviewers (reviewer_refine, reviewer_agent_design, reviewer_plan) work today *because* they ACK with no attestation field. Pitfall 4 in the issue explicitly says: do NOT add models for reviewer_security/reviewer_concurrency unless day-1 ACKs will actually carry attestation. The latent risk: if a future subagent or sandbox helper accidentally attaches a non-empty attestation dict to an ACK from one of the new reviewers and the model is *not* registered, the consensus call raises ValueError and the BRC cycle deadlocks (issue #1925-class symptom).
risks.mitigation: (1) Plan must include an explicit task: "Do not add REVIEWER_ATTESTATION_MODELS entries for reviewer_security or reviewer_concurrency on day 1." (2) Add a unit test in orchestrator/tests/ asserting that an ACK from reviewer_security with attestation=None passes validate_attestation; an ACK from reviewer_security with attestation={...} raises a clear error message naming the role. (3) Document the attestation-skip path in the criteria files so subagents are not encouraged to emit attestation dicts. (4) In a follow-up after #1997 lands and the new reviewers promote to CRITICAL, design and add proper attestation models with strict-mode required fields.
risks.rollback: Trivial: do not register models. If a model is registered prematurely and breaks consensus, deleting the dict entry restores the conditional-attestation skip path.

risks.title: ADVISORY consensus path may be under-tested; new reviewers could deadlock if approval matrix mishandles ADVISORY edges
risks.evidence: orchestrator/review_graph.py exposes critical_reviewers_for() and advisory_reviewers_for() and a demote_edges_for_reviewer() helper. The new reviewers enter as ADVISORY (decision-11). Existing implement-phase ADVISORY reviewers (e.g., documenter→coder) are exercised in current pipelines, but the BRC convergence rule that "missing ADVISORY ACK does not block CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED" is encoded in approval-matrix logic that is easy to mis-edit. If reviewer_security or reviewer_concurrency simply does not respond (sandbox start-up failure, agent crash), the producer must still be able to reach CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED. A regression here would manifest as silent stalls on every implement-phase BRC cycle.
risks.mitigation: (1) Plan must include an integration test under integration_tests/sdlc/ that spawns a reviewer_security agent that exits without ACKing, and asserts the implement-phase BRC still converges via the ADVISORY-skip path. Equivalent test for reviewer_concurrency. (2) Add a smaller unit test of approval_matrix that lists exactly which roles are checked for blocking and confirms reviewer_security/reviewer_concurrency are in the advisory bucket. (3) Verify orchestrator/peer_consensus.py treats CRITICAL vs ADVISORY symmetrically with the reviewer_refine / reviewer_agent_design analogs; if there's existing test coverage of those, mirror it.
risks.rollback: Remove the new ADVISORY edges in review_graph.py — the change is data-only. Pipeline reverts to today's behaviour.

risks.title: Cost / latency multiplier may exceed feedback-1/feedback-2 envelopes for very large PRs
risks.evidence: Feedback-1 accepts 2-5x cost multiplier on large PRs; feedback-2 accepts 5-10 min latency. Decision-3's OR composition (files>10 OR loc>500) means a 12-file 100-LOC PR triggers fan-out, and a 3-file 600-LOC PR also triggers. Default-parallel subagents (decision-6, default true) mean N concurrent Claude calls; each subagent re-runs `git diff` filtered by path glob (decision-4) — for very large diffs (5k+ files) the per-subagent git work is non-trivial. Worst-case unbounded fan-out (e.g., a 50-task implement phase produces 50 subagents) could blow the 5-10 min budget without guardrails.
risks.mitigation: (1) Cap the subagent count in the fan-out prompt — e.g., "never spawn more than 6 subagents; if the partition list exceeds that, group adjacent tasks into a single partition." (2) Suggest a soft guideline in the criteria files: "prefer 3-5 partitions for the typical implement-phase fan-out; only exceed 6 if partitions are completely independent subsystems." (3) Add a smoke benchmark in the regression-replay test (decision-7's RUN_REVIEWER_REPLAY=1 mode) that records wall-clock + token count for the cached PR #1964 fan-out so a future regression is visible. (4) Document the cost ceiling in docs/guides/concurrent-execution.md.
risks.rollback: Pipeline-level: set phase_configs.implement.reviewer_code.parallel=false to serialize subagents; per-prompt-text override: ask the parent reviewer to fall back to solo review. Both knobs already exist by design.

risks.title: Reviewer-criteria drift between SDLC and GHA review surfaces
risks.evidence: shared/prompts/REVIEWER-SYNC.md is the canonical sync guide and explicitly states inline fallbacks must match shared file content. Today's GHA path uses action/build-review-prompt.sh + action/reusable-review.yml; this issue is BRC-internal only (decision-9) and explicitly leaves the GHA reviewer untouched. The implication: starting at this commit, SDLC has reviewer_security and reviewer_concurrency criteria; GHA does not. If a future PR adds wording to security-review-criteria.md without updating REVIEWER-SYNC.md (or the inline fallback in build-review-prompt.sh stays equal to code-review-criteria.md), the two surfaces drift further.
risks.mitigation: (1) The plan must include an explicit REVIEWER-SYNC.md update task that documents the SDLC-only asymmetry — specifically, a new "SDLC-only reviewers" section listing reviewer_security and reviewer_concurrency with a one-line explanation of why GHA does not run them. (2) Add a CI lint that grep-checks REVIEWER-SYNC.md mentions every shared/prompts/*-criteria.md file by name; failure means a new criteria file was added without updating the sync doc. (3) Cross-link the new criteria files back to REVIEWER-SYNC.md in their headers (per decision-5 inheritance pattern, the header already lands; just add the sync-doc link). (4) Plan-reviewer should NACK any plan-phase proposal that touches action/ paths, per the issue body's explicit out-of-scope list.
risks.rollback: REVIEWER-SYNC.md changes are documentation-only — revert restores the prior content. New criteria files can ship even if the sync doc is reverted; the asymmetry simply becomes undocumented (worse, but not broken).

risks.title: Live-LLM regression test (RUN_REVIEWER_REPLAY=1) is non-deterministic; CI baseline drift risk
risks.evidence: Decision-7 ships two modes — CI-unconditional prompt-text asserts plus opt-in live-LLM replay. The live-LLM mode is correct by design (replays PR #1964 and asserts both previously-missed issues are flagged), but live LLMs are non-deterministic; an Anthropic model update could flip a once-passing assertion overnight. If the test is gated only by an env var, it'll be invoked from local dev runs; flakey assertions create a 'runs ok except when it doesn't' confidence-eroding pattern.
risks.mitigation: (1) The live-LLM mode should assert SOFT properties (e.g., "the subagent verdict text mentions sandbox/scripts/jira at least once" or "the verdict mentions ^project$") rather than exact-string outputs. (2) Pin the model version in the test setup to a stable Sonnet snapshot; refresh annually. (3) Track the live-LLM result in a CI artifact (json with token count + assertion outcomes) so flakes are visible historically. (4) Make the live-LLM test idempotent (no side effects, no committed state changes) and call it out in the test docstring as `flaky-by-design`. (5) The prompt-asserts mode (always-on) covers the regression: that the reviewer prompt actually contains the subagent block at the right threshold. That is the structural guarantee.
risks.rollback: If live-LLM flake noise drowns signal, deprecate the live-LLM mode and keep prompt-asserts only. No on-disk schema impact.

risks.title: phase_configs.implement.reviewer_code.parallel field is a new contract schema element; older contracts and persisted-state migrations risk
risks.evidence: Decision-6 places the parallelism knob at phase_configs.implement.reviewer_code.parallel. shared/egg_contracts/models.py:499 already declares phase_configs as Optional[dict[PipelinePhase, PhaseConfig]] and shared/egg_contracts/phase_defaults.py:132 has a `phase_configs is None` defaults path. So additive fields under PhaseConfig are schema-friendly. But .egg-state/contracts/*.json contains 100+ persisted contracts from prior pipelines without this field; deserializing them with a new strict-mode pydantic field (e.g., required) would fail. Risk is low because PhaseConfig has historically used optional fields.
risks.mitigation: (1) Plan task must specify: add the new field as Optional[bool] with default None on PhaseConfig (or its reviewer-config sub-model); resolve as `True` (parallel) when None. Test with at least one persisted contract from the .egg-state/contracts/ tree. (2) Add a unit test that loads issue-1965.json (this very pipeline) post-implementation and asserts default-parallel behaviour. (3) Bump schemaVersion in .egg/schemas/contract.schema.json with a non-breaking note. (4) Surface the knob in docs/guides/sdlc-pipeline.md briefly so operators know it exists.
risks.rollback: Remove the field from the model — revert is straightforward, no data migration since the field is optional and additive.

risks.title: Prompt injection from hostile diff content is amplified in fan-out review
risks.evidence: Today's reviewer_code reads the entire diff in one context and may be prompt-injected by content the diff places in the model's context (e.g., a malicious string disguised as instructions inside a test file). Fan-out N-multiplies the prompt-injection surface: each subagent reads its slice of the diff in a fresh context. A successful injection in one subagent could yield a spurious ACK from that subagent only; per the verdict-merging rule, the parent then ACKs unless another subagent NACKs the same area. Egg pipelines run only on internal repos today, so this is largely theoretical, but BRC-confirmed implement-phase changes go directly to PR — a hostile contributor (in a fork PR scenario) could exploit this if the pipeline is ever pointed at fork branches.
risks.mitigation: (1) Subagent prompts should include a fixed preamble (already inherited from code-review-criteria.md) instructing the agent to treat diff content as data, not instructions. (2) Verdict-merging rule should require at least two subagents to ACK the same partition before the partition counts as approved — i.e., redundant coverage on overlapping path globs would reduce single-subagent injection wins. This is a future enhancement; not needed day 1. (3) Add a security-review-criteria.md note on prompt-injection awareness for the new reviewer_security agent specifically. (4) Track the prompt-injection threat model in a follow-up issue tied to fork-PR support; mark out-of-scope for v1.
risks.rollback: Disable fan-out (phase_configs flag). Solo-reviewer path has the same prompt-injection risk that exists today, no worse.

risks.title: phases.implement.tasks[] partition strategy fails when contract task descriptions are vague or missing
risks.evidence: Decision-2 routes the reviewer to fetch implement-phase tasks via mcp__sdlc__show_contract. Tasks are typically authored by task_planner and may be vague (e.g., "add tests", "update docs") or absent for custom-phase invocations. If tasks are vague, the reviewer may still partition but the partitions don't map cleanly to changed-file directories, defeating the per-subagent path-glob filter (decision-4). Result: subagents review overlapping or empty slices, wasting cost and missing coverage.
risks.mitigation: (1) The reviewer prompt fallback (already specified in decision-2) — when implement-phase tasks list is empty, skip fan-out — should extend to: when tasks are present but partition extraction yields fewer than 2 distinct path globs, fall back to per-directory partitioning of the diff. (2) Add a fixture-based unit test with a contract whose tasks are all `add tests` and assert the reviewer falls back to directory partitioning. (3) Long term, encourage task_planner to include `affected_paths` hints on each implement-phase task — separate spin-off issue.
risks.rollback: Pipeline-level: set the new parallel flag to false. Or revert the fan-out block in pipelines.py.

risks.title: Regression-replay fixture (1964-diff.patch) bloats the integration-tests tree and may go stale
risks.evidence: Feedback-12 specifies a cached PR #1964 diff fixture committed to integration_tests/sdlc/fixtures/. PR #1964 was a Jira-wrapper change; the diff is sizeable but bounded. Fixture files committed to git become permanent (history rewrite is the only delete). If the test eventually moves on to other regression PRs, old fixtures accumulate. Additionally, if PR #1964 is later restructured or deleted upstream, the fixture is the only remaining record — fine for the test, slight risk for traceability.
risks.mitigation: (1) Cap the fixture size to a reasonable byte budget — e.g., < 200 KB total — by trimming context lines or storing as a slim patch. (2) Document the fixture's provenance in a README inside integration_tests/sdlc/fixtures/ pointing back to PR #1964 + commit SHA. (3) Plan the test as one of N future regression replays — consider a fixtures/<issue-num>/ subdirectory layout. (4) Periodic cleanup is a low-priority follow-up.
risks.rollback: git rm the fixture file, delete the test. No production impact.

risks.title: MCP availability inside Task subagent contexts is unverified — could break decision-2's self-fetch path
risks.evidence: Risk-3 and risk-4 both touch this; calling out separately for clarity. The Claude Agent SDK's Task tool spawns a child agent with a fresh tool registry; whether that registry inherits the parent's MCP servers (mcp__brc__, mcp__sdlc__, mcp__phase__, etc.) is configuration-dependent. shared/egg_agent/client.py does not show explicit per-subagent MCP server passing. If subagents do *not* inherit MCP, decision-2's plan (reviewer self-fetches the contract) cannot work — the parent has to fetch and pass it in via the subagent prompt, which is essentially option 3A by another route.
risks.mitigation: (1) Mandatory pre-implementation spike (per risk-4): confirm Task subagents in the egg sandbox have mcp__sdlc__show_contract reachable. If not, escalate to the architect / refiner: this changes decision-2 from 3B to 3A. (2) The plan task that adds the subagent block should include the MCP-availability assertion as part of its acceptance criteria — either "subagent successfully calls mcp__sdlc__show_contract" or "parent passes contract.implement.tasks[] in the subagent prompt as a fallback". (3) If MCP is *not* available, the subagent design simplifies — parent does all MCP work, slices the contract data, and passes per-subagent partition specs via prompt only. Also covers risk-12's fallback path.
risks.rollback: Switch decisions 2 and 4 to parent-side data flow (option 3A + parent pre-slicing). The new ADVISORY reviewers and criteria files remain useful even if subagent fan-out collapses to a parent-side loop.

risks.title: Threshold composition ambiguity in OR mode: small refactors trip fan-out without justifying the cost
risks.evidence: Decision-3 chose OR composition (files>10 OR loc>500). A typescript rename refactor that touches 12 files for ~30 LOC trips the file count and triggers full fan-out. A 3-file CSS replacement of 700 LOC trips the LOC count. Both are mechanical low-risk changes that don't benefit from the security/concurrency lens. Cost feedback-1 (2-5x acceptable) absorbs this, but the gain is zero.
risks.mitigation: (1) Acceptable as designed; this risk is informational. (2) If post-launch telemetry shows >30 percent of fan-outs fire on mechanical refactors, consider a v2 refinement: AND composition for trivial-file-type heuristics (e.g., import-only changes, rename-only commits) using `git diff --shortstat` patterns. (3) Document the OR composition in docs/architecture/orchestrator.md as a deliberate v1 simplification.
risks.rollback: Switch composition to AND in the prompt text. Single-line change.

risks.title: BRC heartbeat / liveness signal drops if subagents block the parent's event loop
risks.evidence: egg-orch heartbeat / progress emission is per-agent. The parent reviewer_code is the heartbeat-emitting role; if it spawns N subagents and awaits their output, the parent's heartbeats stop until the slowest subagent returns. orchestrator's stuck-phase-transition / agent-heartbeat-stall overseer alerts (issue #2012) gate on Tier-1 signals — long subagent runs could trip the gate. Issue #2036 explicitly addressed this for mcp__brc__wait_loop, but the in-Claude-loop case (Task tool blocking) is not the same thing.
risks.mitigation: (1) Document an explicit per-subagent timeout in the prompt (e.g., 5 min hard cap per subagent), well below the parent's heartbeat-stall threshold. (2) Have the parent emit a pre-fan-out STATUS message before invoking Task and a post-fan-out STATUS message after — this gives observability even when heartbeats are quiescent. (3) The pre-implementation spike (risk-4) should record parent heartbeat behaviour during a real fan-out and confirm the orchestrator does not raise overseer alerts. (4) If the SDK supports streamed subagent results, prefer that; otherwise document the gap.
risks.rollback: Disable parallel fan-out; serialize subagent calls (one at a time) to ensure parent loop stays interactive between calls.

risks.title: Day-1 ADVISORY criticality means new reviewers may go silent without anyone noticing
risks.evidence: Decision-11 places both reviewers in ADVISORY. ADVISORY ACKs/NACKs are recorded but cannot deadlock consensus — and missing ADVISORY ACKs are by definition non-blocking. So a sandbox-misconfigured reviewer_security that simply never starts will not stall pipelines. Without dedicated telemetry, no operator notices. The pipeline 'looks fine' but in fact the new lens never ran; we're back to 1964-class blind spots.
risks.mitigation: (1) Track ADVISORY reviewer ACK/NACK rates in pipeline telemetry from day 1 — even a simple counter scraped from BRC history that says `pipelines where reviewer_security ACKed: M / N`. (2) Add a docs note in docs/guides/concurrent-execution.md: "reviewer_security and reviewer_concurrency are ADVISORY for the first N pipelines; verify they are actually firing by checking BRC history." (3) Plan a follow-up issue to flip them to CRITICAL after #1997 ships and after telemetry shows >95 percent ACK/NACK rate. (4) Tied to risk-2's STATUS message instrumentation — same logging mechanism applies.
risks.rollback: n/a — this is an operational visibility risk, not a code path. Mitigation is logging.

risks.title: PIPE-internal reviewer additions could mask issues the GHA reviewer would still catch — no net regression but no net win either
risks.evidence: The acceptance target (decision-9) is trend-based: GHA blocking-count per pipeline-PR trends to zero. If reviewer_security/reviewer_concurrency catch and route fixes inside the pipeline, the GHA blocking-count drops — success. If they fail to catch (e.g., still miss the ^project$ class of bug), the GHA reviewer catches and the trend stalls. Either way, the system continues working; this is success-criteria risk, not correctness risk.
risks.mitigation: (1) The decision-7 regression test directly checks the historical PR #1964 blockers; passing the test means the new lenses do catch *those* bugs. Doesn't guarantee future bugs are caught, but provides a regression floor. (2) Track decision-9's blocking-count trend in a simple dashboard — e.g., a script that scrapes the last 20 pipeline-produced PRs from GitHub and counts blocking GHA review comments. (3) Plan a follow-up review at N=20 PRs to assess whether the trend is moving; if not, revisit the criteria-file content.
risks.rollback: n/a — this is a measurement / evaluation risk, not a code-path risk.

risks.title: Cross-partition findings missed when bug spans subagent boundaries — directly reproduces the PR #1964 ^project$ failure mode
risks.evidence: Architect (R-8) calls this out independently: decision-4 has each subagent re-run `git diff` filtered by path glob to its assigned partition. If a route handler in partition A has its allowlist extractor in partition B, no single subagent sees the handler-vs-validator mismatch; the parent reviewer also does not necessarily perform an end-to-end pass over the whole diff. This is *exactly* the ^project$ information-disclosure bug pattern that issue #1965 is designed to prevent. The architect's mitigation (a parent end-to-end final pass) is not yet binding because it lives in prose only.
risks.mitigation: (1) Plan must specify that the parent reviewer_code prompt explicitly mandates a parent-side cross-partition end-to-end pass *after* subagents complete. The pass need not be exhaustive; it should focus on cross-file invariants (handler ↔ allowlist consistency, route ↔ schema consistency, fixture ↔ Dockerfile reference consistency). (2) reviewer_security's criteria file (security-review-criteria.md) should call out cross-file allowlist-vs-handler checks as a first-class lens — explicitly mention the ^project$ pattern. (3) The regression-replay test (decision-7) must assert that *either* a subagent or the parent flagged the ^project$ issue *and* the broken sandbox/scripts/jira symlink. If only one of the two is flagged, the test fails and the prompt design is revisited. (4) Document this risk in docs/architecture/orchestrator.md as the canonical reason for the parent-side post-pass.
risks.rollback: Disable subagent fan-out (phase_configs flag) — solo-reviewer path retains the full-diff context and avoids the partition-boundary blind spot at the cost of feedback-1's accepted 2-5x token reduction goal. Acceptable rollback if the regression-replay test fails post-launch.

human_review_areas.why: First production use of Claude Agent SDK Task tool inside egg. Pre-implementation smoke spike (described in risks 4, 14, 16) needs human judgment on outcome — go-no-go decision on decision-2/decision-4 may flip from option B to option A.
blocking_open_questions_for_humans: Are MCP servers reachable from Task subagents in the egg sandbox?
Does the parent reviewer's BRC heartbeat continue while subagents run?
Do subagents inherit EGG_AGENT_ROLE / cwd / write-block enforcement correctly?

human_review_areas.why: If parent ACK iff every subagent ACK, a single subagent's failure to load context fails the whole review. If parent ACK on majority subagent ACK, single-subagent prompt-injection (risk-11) could pass through. Need explicit human decision before implementation.

rollback_plan_summary: Three layered rollback handles: (1) flip phase_configs.implement.reviewer_code.parallel to false on the contract — disables subagent fan-out without code change. (2) Revert the prompt-text change in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py — pure prompt edit, no schema or migration. (3) git rm the new reviewer roles from agent_roles.py and review_graph.py edges — data-only. Each layer is independent; you can disable fan-out without rolling back the new ADVISORY reviewers, and vice versa.
